correctness.rationale: The circular-gap layers partition the pairs. In each ordinary layer the potential values are (k−1)n+1 through kn; the even diametrical top layer has h instead of n entries. Letter a reduces the potential by one except at the layer heads, where the start index wraps. Letter b is the identity off pairs containing n−1. On {r,n−1} it reduces the potential by one for r=0 through h−1 (the first case merges); for the remaining r it raises it by n, except at the odd midpoint r=h where it raises it by h. Thus exactly one letter reduces the potential by one, neither can reduce it faster, and all minimal words follow the forced path down through the layers. This proves the formula, the suffix labels and both master words, including n=2 (the unique word is b). Fresh time-layer tabulation of all states and shortest word multiplicities at n=2..25 in /workspace/reproductions/34_pairs_and_rings.py agreed exactly. Frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected, not run.

evidence: A maximal pair distance N=binomial(n,2) implies spectrum {1,…,N}, since any longest optimal path visits every pair without repetition and all suffixes are optimal. The weighted result identifies the unique equality letter and shows that every distance occurs on one pair.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The published extremal fact alone is not a display of explicit pair labels or letters. In this particular automaton, the additional observation that a(P) and b(P) are distinct on every unmerged pair already makes geodesic letters unique once each positive rank has a single state (at rank one only b can merge). More decisively, tracing the indexed equality policy with unit weights gives n−1 a-steps then b in each complete gap layer, and h−1 a-steps then b at the top even layer. The proposed master expression therefore does not add a separate invariant.
